Rashi on Megillah 28b:10:1.english: He said: Whether due to my honor [or] whether due to the honor of the deceased - it is a public eulogy:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:11:1.english: Who used to teach halakhah - [Meaning] that he would teach Mishnayot to students.

Rashi on Megillah 28b:11:2.hebrew: בכ"ד שורות - של תלמידים:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:11:3.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "חסרא ליה ארעא דישראל גברא רבה":
Rashi on Megillah 28b:11:3.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Eretz Yisrael has lost [*chasra leih*] a great man":

Rashi on Megillah 28b:12:1.english: How shall I eulogize [him] - With what shall I eulogize him:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:12:2.hebrew: הי צנא מלא סיפרי - אינו אלא כסל שמילאוהו ספרים, ואין מבין מה בתוכה; אף שונה הלכות ולא שימש ת"ח ללמוד שיבינוהו טעמי משנה, ופעמים שדברי משנה סותרין זה את זה וצריך לתרצה — כגון "הכא במאי עסקינן", וכגון "הא מני רבי פלוני היא", וכגון "חסורי מיחסרא" — אינו יודע מה שונה:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:12:2.english: Alas, a basket full of books - [He] is nothing more than a basket that they have filled with books, which does not understand what is inside it; so too, one who recites halakhot [by rote] and has not attended upon Torah scholars to learn [from them] so that they might make him understand the reasons of the Mishnah, and [where] at times the words of the Mishnah contradict one another and one must reconcile them — such as "With what [case] are we dealing here?", and such as "Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi So-and-so", and such as "[The Mishnah] is missing [words]" — [such a person] does not know what he is reciting:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:13:1.hebrew: תקיפי ארעא דישראל - ריש לקיש, דאמרינן במסכת יומא (דף ט:) דאפילו בהדי רבה בר בר חנה לא משתעי, דמאן דמשתעי בהדי ריש לקיש בשוקא — יהבין ליה עיסקא בלא סהדי: רב נחמן בר יצחק מחסידי בבל, בשילהי מסכת סוטה (דף מט:), דקאמר ליה: "לא תתני יראת חטא, דאיכא אנא":
Rashi on Megillah 28b:13:1.english: The forceful ones of the Land of Israel - [This refers to] Reish Lakish, about whom we say in Tractate Yoma (9b) that he would not even converse with Rabbah bar bar Channah, for anyone who conversed with Reish Lakish in the marketplace would be given merchandise [on trust] without witnesses. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak [was one] of the pious ones of Babylonia, [as seen] at the end of Tractate Sotah (49b), where he said to him [the reciter of the Mishnah]: "Do not teach [that] fear of sin [has ceased], for there is me":

Rashi on Megillah 28b:14:1.english: With the taga - [meaning] the crown of the Torah:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:14:2.english: Will perish - Passes from the world:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:15:1.english: Urkema demaya - A puddle of gathered water:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:16:1.english: That I may serve him - that I may serve my master:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:16:2.hebrew: שהחמירו על עצמן - דמדאורייתא אין צריכה שבעה נקיים אלא הרואה שלושה ימים רצופים בתוך י"א יום שבין נדה לנדה, אבל בתחלת נדתה, אפילו ראתה כל שבעה ופסקה לערב, טובלת בלילה. והן החמירו על עצמן לפי שאין הכל בקיאים בפתח נדתה, אימתי הן עומדות בי"א ימים שבין נדה לנדה. ואם תאמר: לא יחמירו אלא בג' רצופין, כדכתיב: "ימים רבים בלא עת נדתה" (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ה)? פעמים שראיית דם נדה מזקיקתה לשבעה נקיים מן התורה. כיצד? התחילה לספור שבעה נקיים לאחר שהיתה זבה גמורה, וספרה שבעה נקיים, ובשביעי ראתה אפי' כחרדל — סתרה הכל וצריכה לחזור ולספור שבעה נקיים. אי נמי, שמא ראתה שני ימים ולא ידעה, והיום ראתה וידעה, דהוו להו שלשה ימים רצופין וצריכה שבעה נקיים, ועל כן החמירו:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:16:2.english: They were strict upon themselves - For by Torah law, [a woman] does not require seven clean [days] except one who sees [blood for] three consecutive days within the eleven days between [one] menstrual period and the next. However, at the beginning of her menstrual period, even if she saw [blood] all seven [days] and ceased [before] evening, she immerses at night. And they were strict upon themselves because not everyone is expert in [calculating] the start of her menstrual period, [to know] when they are within the eleven days between [one] menstrual period and the next. And if you should say: Let them only be strict [for] three consecutive [days], as it is written, "many days outside the time of her menstrual impurity" (Leviticus 15:25)? Sometimes a sighting of menstrual blood obligates her in seven clean [days] by Torah law. How so? [If] she began to count seven clean [days] after she was a major *zavah* [a woman who had three consecutive days of non-menstrual discharge], and she counted seven clean [days] and on the seventh she saw [even a drop] like a mustard seed — she has nullified all [of them] and must go back and count seven clean [days]. Alternatively, perhaps she saw [blood] for two days and did not know, and today she saw [it] and knew, so that they are three consecutive days and she requires seven clean [days], and therefore they were strict:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:1:1.hebrew: ואין ניאותין - ואין מתקשטין לתוכו, ואין מטיילין שם:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:1:1.english: And one may not adorn oneself - And they do not adorn themselves inside it, and they do not stroll there:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:1:2.hebrew: הספד של רבים - של תלמיד חכם שמת, שצריכין להתאסף ולהספידו, ובית הכנסת ראוי לכך לפי שהוא בית גדול:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:1:2.english: A public eulogy - [A eulogy] of a Torah scholar who died, [for] whom [people] must gather and eulogize him, and the synagogue is suitable for this because it is a large building:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:3:1.english: Who mentioned their name? - Where did we hear the Tanna Kamma [say] to do something in them that prevents grass from sprouting?

Rashi on Megillah 28b:3:2.hebrew: אימתי - מכבדין ומרביצין אותן? ביישובן. לאחר שמכבדין, מזלפין את המים להרביץ את האבק:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:3:2.english: When - [do they] sweep and sprinkle them? When they are occupied. After they sweep, they sprinkle water to settle the dust:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:4:1.english: With a stipulation - on condition that they may use them:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:5:1.english: They keep [a corpse] in it overnight - [This] implies that it is an obligation to keep a corpse in it overnight:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:5:2.english: Ultimately they will keep unattended corpses [metei mitzvah] overnight in it - [meaning] that people will die in the city who have no one to bury them:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:6:1.hebrew: מאי בי רבנן - למה קורין בתי מדרשות בי רבנן? לפי שביתם הוא לכל דבר:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:6:1.english: What [is] Bei Rabbanan - why do they call study halls Bei Rabbanan [house of the Sages]? Because it is their home for every matter:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:7:1.english: A shower of rain [zilḥa de-mitra] - A stream of water that comes with force:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:7:2.hebrew: לאו משום מיטרא - שיגן עלינו מפני הגשמים, שאם לא היינו עוסקין בשמעתא, לא היינו נכנסין:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:7:2.english: Not due to the rain - [meaning] that it should shelter us from the rain, for if we were not engaged in [studying] the halakha, we would not have entered:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:7:3.hebrew: צילותא - דעת צלולה ומיושבת, שאינו טרוד בכלום מחשבה:
Rashi on Megillah 28b:7:3.english: Clarity - a clear and settled mind, [such] that one is not distracted by any thought:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:8:1.english: If a person needs to call a man from the synagogue, what should one do? - Since one may not enter them [synagogues] without a [valid] need:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:8:2.english: Let him say to a child - for the children were accustomed to read [Scripture] in the synagogue:

Rashi on Megillah 28b:9:1.english: For example, a eulogy that takes place in the academy of Rav Sheshet - [That is,] if one person in the academy of Rav Sheshet dies:

Tosafot on Megillah 28b:16:1.hebrew: שאפילו רואות טפת דם כחרדל יושבות עליה שבעה נקיים - ולא קשיא מהא דאמר בנדה (דף סו.) ובפרק יוצא דופן (נדה ד' מג.) שאפילו כעין חרדל טמא, דשמא התם לא מיירי להצריכה שבעה נקיים, אלא להיות נדה דאורייתא. וקשיא: היאך מצינו טפה כחרדל הגורמת שבעה נקיים בדאורייתא, דודאי לא תקנו חכמים דבר דלית דכוותה דאורייתא? ויש לומר דאשכחנא בה שפיר בז' לספירתה, שסותרת הכל:
Tosafot on Megillah 28b:16:1.english: That even if they see a drop of blood [the size] of a mustard seed, they wait on its account seven clean [days] - And there is no difficulty from that which is stated in Niddah (66a) and in the chapter [entitled] Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 43a), that even [a drop] like a mustard seed is impure, because perhaps there it is not speaking of requiring her [to observe] seven clean [days], but rather of becoming a niddah under Torah law. And it is difficult: how do we find a drop [the size] of a mustard seed that causes [the requirement of] seven clean [days] under Torah law, for certainly the Sages did not enact something that has no counterpart in Torah law? And one can say that we indeed find [such a case] with it on the seventh [day] of her counting, where it invalidates everything:

Tosafot on Megillah 28b:4:1.hebrew: בתי כנסיות של בבל על תנאי הן עשויין - רוצה לומר: כל זמן שהן בטלין, דהא חזינן בברייתא דלעיל, וגם שהאמוראים לא היו רוצים ליכנס בהן בגשמים מפני גשמים, אלא משום דשמעתא בעי צילותא; והכא מיירי כשחרב, דאז מהני התנאי. ודווקא לאותן שבבבל מהני התנאי, שהרי לעת בא גואל במהרה בימינו תפקע קדושתן; אבל לאותן שבארץ ישראל לא מהני תנאי, שהרי קדושתן לעולם קיימת. וא"ת: כיון דמהני תנאי לאותן שבבבל, א"כ קשה מההיא דלעיל (מגילה דף כו:), דרבינא דהוה ליה בי כנישתא בארעיה, ואמר ליה רב אשי: זיל זבנה משבעה טובי העיר — ואמאי איצטריך לעשות כן אחר שנחרב? וי"ל: משום דזרעה, דזריעה הוי קלות ראש ביותר ועגמת נפש, ומשום הכי אסור אפי' בחורבנה:
Tosafot on Megillah 28b:4:1.english: Synagogues of Babylonia are built with a stipulation - That is to say: [only] for the time that they are in disuse — for indeed we saw in the baraita above, and also that the Amoraim did not want to enter them during the rains because of the rain, but rather because a halakhic discussion requires clarity [of mind]; and here [our Gemara] is dealing with when it has been destroyed, for then the stipulation is effective. And specifically for those in Babylonia is the stipulation effective, for at the time the Redeemer comes, speedily in our days, their sanctity will cease; but for those in the Land of Israel a stipulation is not effective, for their sanctity endures forever. And if you ask: since a stipulation is effective for those in Babylonia, if so, there is a difficulty from that [incident] above (Megillah 26b) concerning Ravina, who had a synagogue on his land, and Rav Ashi said to him, "Go buy it from the seven townspeople" — why was it necessary to do so after it was destroyed? One can answer: because he sowed it, for sowing is extreme frivolity and anguish, and therefore it is forbidden even in its ruin:

Tosafot on Megillah 28b:4:2.hebrew: ואעפ"כ אין נוהגין בהן קלות ראש - פירוש, בבנינה, שהרי בחורבנה שרי בכל הני. ואצטריך לאשמועינן, משום דסלקא דעתך אמינא דדווקא אכילה ושתיה, דהוי קלות ראש ביותר, הוא דאסור, אבל חשבונות, דלא הוי קלות ראש כל כך, סלקא דעתך אמינא דשריא — קמ"ל דלא:
Tosafot on Megillah 28b:4:2.english: But nevertheless, they do not act inside them with frivolity - Meaning, while [the synagogue] is standing, for when it is in ruins, all of these [activities] are permitted. And it was necessary to teach us [this], because you might have thought to say that specifically eating and drinking, which is extreme frivolity, is what is forbidden, whereas [making] calculations, which is not so much frivolity, you might have thought to say is permitted — [therefore] it teaches us that [it is] not:
